dense_er_scaling.description: Dense Erdos-Renyi polymatrix games. The paper reports that the proposed private equilibrium finder lowers exploitability and Renyi-DP budget as the number of players grows.

cce_decreases_with_n.description: Rewards methods whose CCE exploitability improves as dense problem size grows.

privacy_decreases_with_n.description: Rewards methods whose evaluated Renyi-DP budget improves as dense problem size grows.

competitive_with_baseline.description: Checks that the method's exploitability is not worse than the noisy-OMD baseline by more than the allowed tolerance.

cce_exploitability_mean.description: Mean CCE exploitability on the evaluated slice; lower values indicate better equilibrium quality.

privacy_budget_mean.description: Mean Renyi-DP privacy budget on the evaluated slice; lower values preserve the paper's privacy constraint.

final_nash_gap_mean.description: Mean final-iterate Nash gap, a secondary equilibrium-quality check against shortcut trajectories.

baseline_cce_ratio.description: Mean CCE exploitability divided by the noisy-OMD baseline at matched player counts.

strategy_simplex_violation_mean.description: Mean violation of probability-simplex constraints in saved trajectories; lower values catch invalid shortcut artifacts.

dense_cluster_scaling.description: Dense clustered polymatrix games from Appendix D.1. The reported qualitative result is decreasing exploitability and privacy budget with player count.

cce_decreases_with_n.description: Rewards methods whose CCE exploitability improves as dense clustered problem size grows.
